profile.summary: AMPLIFY is a protein language model. It reads a protein amino acid sequence and returns per-residue and per-protein embeddings and masked-token logits, which can be used as features for property prediction or to suggest mutations. It comes in two sizes, 120M and 350M parameters, and the authors released the training code, data and checkpoints.
profile.summary_source_locator: model card: AMPLIFY; README: introduction; docs usage.rst: Inference

summary_quotes.text: AMPLIFY is an efficient, state-of-the-art protein language model pre-trained using masked language modeling on UniRef100, OAS, and SCOP
AMPLIFY can generate residue and protein embeddings, suggest mutations, differentiate disordered proteins from non-protein sequences, and much more.
AMPLIFY is available in two sizes, 120M and 350M parameters, with the `_base` models not extended beyond 512 residues (Stage 1).
we have open-sourced AMPLIFY's pre-training codebase, data, and model checkpoints.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: AMPLIFY is a transformer encoder trained with masked language modelling: 15% of residues are masked and the model learns to predict them. The layers use rotary position embeddings, SwiGLU activations and RMS normalisation, with no bias terms in the attention or feed-forward layers. Training ran in two stages. Stage 1 ran for 1,000,000 steps on sequences of up to 512 residues. Stage 2 extended the length to 2048 for 25,000 steps (120M) or 50,000 steps (350M). The authors frame the work around data quality rather than scale: they argue that sequence databases are a biased sample of the fitness landscape and built a curated training set, UR100P.
sections.source_locator: model card: Model Descritpion and Training Descritpion tables; README: introduction

quotes.text: the premise that scale leads to better performance assumes that source databases provide accurate representation of the underlying fitness landscape, which is likely false
addressing data quality concerns such as sample bias

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four checkpoints are on Hugging Face and Zenodo: AMPLIFY_350M and AMPLIFY_120M are the final models, and AMPLIFY_350M_base and AMPLIFY_120M_base are the Stage 1 models, not extended beyond 512 residues. The two sizes differ in width and depth (640 hidden units and 24 layers against 960 and 32). The training datasets are also published, downloaded in December 2023 and processed with the repository's data pipeline. A result should name the checkpoint and the Hugging Face revision; this page read AMPLIFY_350M at revision 223e35e4. The repository code was read at commit 7fb657a6.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Masked protein language model (encoder) that produces embeddings and residue logits.

quotes.text: AMPLIFY is an efficient, state-of-the-art protein language model pre-trained using masked language modeling on UniRef100, OAS, and SCOP

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with rotary embeddings (theta 10000), SwiGLU, RMS norm and no attention or feed-forward biases. AMPLIFY 120M: hidden size 640, 24 layers, 10 heads. AMPLIFY 350M: hidden size 960, 32 layers, 15 heads.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Protein amino acid sequences, tokenised with a 27-token vocabulary.

run_guide.summary: Install the AMPLIFY package from the pinned commit and embed one protein with the AMPLIFY_350M checkpoint from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU: the example moves the model to the GPU because of Flash Attention.
Internet access to Hugging Face for the weights and the UR100P dataset.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/chandar-lab/AMPLIFY
cd AMPLIFY
git checkout --detach 7fb657a6bd411e0d51517ccde7cc35391c072b65
export REPO_DIR=$(pwd)
steps.explanation: Clones the official repository and pins it to the commit read for this page. The clone and checkout lines and the REPO_DIR export are added by Rewire; the README's install command expects REPO_DIR to point at the clone.

steps.title: Embed one protein
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModel
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from datasets import load_dataset

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("chandar-lab/AMPLIFY_350M", trust_remote_code=True)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("chandar-lab/AMPLIFY_350M", trust_remote_code=True)
model = model.to("cuda")

dataset = load_dataset("chandar-lab/UR100P", data_dir="UniProt", split="test")

for sample in dataset:
    print("Sample: ", sample["name"], sample["sequence"])
    input = tokenizer.encode(sample["sequence"], return_tensors="pt")
    print("Input: ", input)
    input = input.to("cuda")
    output = model(input)
    print("Output: ", output)
    break
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's Get Started example, wrapped in a shell heredoc by Rewire with its comments removed. It downloads AMPLIFY_350M and one sample from the UR100P UniProt test split and runs one forward pass on the GPU.

outputs: The script prints the sample name and sequence, the token IDs, and the model output object for one UniProt test protein.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and model card and have not been executed by Rewire.

The model card does not say what the output object contains; the repository's Predictor class (docs usage.rst) gives logits and embeddings but loads checkpoints from local files, not from Hugging Face.
The card example does not pin a Hugging Face revision; this page read revision 223e35e4.
